title: Record the tutor-signals route, its loader key, the five states the pane renders and the absence it states
question: which route reaches the tutor-signals surface, which LOADERS key resolves it, what does each of the five states the pane renders read off the answer the shipped join gave, and in which sentence is the ordering stated as the named absence?

measuredAt: static: every citation below was read out of the file it names at the head above and re-resolved by searching that file for the exact line it quotes rather than by trusting a typed number; the answer the record states is `extension/tutor-signals.js` run node-side in a bare `node:vm` context over `research/raw/m039-render-phase.json`’s `/effect/freshRead`, printed by the `measurement` command below. route.name: tutor-signals
route.statement: one entry of the `PANEL_SURFACES` list (:84), spread into the `appRoutes` table by the one mapped literal the table ends with, lazy through the shared `loadPanelDemo` closure the table defines once (:14, :15), and naming its surface in `data.surface` (:147) as every demo-backed route does. It sits directly after `tutor-foundations` (:83) rather than after `what-changed`, for the reason the list’s own note states: every citation of `m047`..`m055` and of `scripts/component-search.test.mjs` is pinned to its line, so an entry appended at the end would move them. The entry cost the list one line and moved no cited line, because M057’s T004 folded the M053 note’s two lines into one to pay for it (PLAN C3): `console-read` (:78), `copy-check` (:95), `interaction-story` (:98) and `dead-click` (:104) keep their numbers, and so does the `appRoutes` declaration (:113). The route registers nothing and measures nothing: it reaches the pane that renders the join’s answer.

loader.statement: the `tutor-signals` key is the last entry of the `LOADERS` map (:35, :65), and it is the only path to `panel-tutor-signals.ts`: the demo looks the key up by the name the route’s `data.surface` states (:717), awaits the dynamic import (:723), calls the module’s default export with the sample fact (:724), and sets the state (:725) and the lines (:726) the module answers. The fact is entered after the component rather than inside the `FACTS` literal, because every cited line of that literal is pinned by `m048`..`m055` and a fact added up there would move them (the comment above it says so). The one line the key itself cost is paid for by the blank line M057’s T007 removed between the map and that literal, so the eight surface records which pin this file’s lines re-resolve at this head instead of being re-cited. The fact is the join’s own answer over the record T003 pins — `state: answered`, the effect node at index 5 with the empty label, the one upstream node at index 2 labelled `count`, no unplaced reference, and the ordering as `no-write-record-no-order` — and `panel-demo.spec.ts` re-reads that record, evaluates the shipped join from its committed text and holds this fact to that answer field for field, so a fact that drifted reddens there rather than shipping.

answer.statement: the pane is the display half and reads only these fields: it reads no record, opens no page, stats no file, dispatches no message, asks nothing of an inspected window and imports nothing at runtime, so the join’s rules are never restated here as a computation. The answer itself is the join’s: `tutorSignals` (:589) reads the graph record (:596), the render/effect entry (:610), the effect node the entry names (:625) and the upstream nodes its edges state (:655), and every field the pane prints is one the join carried from a record’s own field. The answer this record states is the join’s own over `research/raw/m039-render-phase.json`’s `/effect/freshRead` and not a page read: no capture was taken by this milestone (PLAN C8), and the same answer is re-derived node-side by `panel-demo.spec.ts` on every test run.

In this record it renders the empty label beside `index: 5` and the one upstream node `count` at `index: 2` — the measurement above is that answer — and it names no write, no owner and no cause (SC1, SC2; E1, E2, E7).

states.statement: the pane’s own absence, not one of the join’s four: no answer was handed to it at all, or the value it was handed is no object or carries no `state` word (:399-:401). It reads no field — there is none to read — and states the absence in its own sentence, which is why a surface handed nothing renders a sentence rather than a blank pane, and why the word is no synonym for any of the three absences.

sentenceAt.lineText: text: 'ordering: the record carries no write record, so the ordering between a write and this render is the named absence no-write-record-no-order — an edge is a direction of dependency and holds no field, no value and no moment to read an order out of — and this pane names no write, no owner and no cause',

absence.why: no write record exists anywhere in `extension/` — T001 measured it and recorded it in `research/raw/m057-record-shapes.json` — and an edge is a direction of dependency that carries no field, no value and no moment (`extension/render-phase.js:18`), so a write is not representable in one and no ordering can be read out of a direction. The absence is therefore stated and not captured: there is no field in the answer a cause could sit in.
absence.statement: the ordering is one object — `{ state: ’absent’, absence: ’no-write-record-no-order’ }` — built in exactly one place in the join (:446) and carried on every answer, including the three absences (:493), so no branch of the join can vary it. The pane renders the sentence registered as `ordering-absent` (:196) and then the object’s own two fields (:422-:423), and names no write, no owner and no cause anywhere (SC2). The measured answer above carries the absence as its `ordering` field, which is the same object this record names.

notCaptured: Nothing here was rendered, clicked or captured: every value is a static read of the files the `sources` block names, at the head above, and the answer the record states is the shipped join run node-side over a record already on disk. No browser was opened, no page was read, no profiler was tapped and no `serializeGraph` call was made (PLAN C8).

No page read produced this answer and none could: `extension/agent-main.js:958` pushes `id: String(n.id)` and resolves each edge end to a node id, so a fresh `serializeGraph` capture reproduces the missing-`index` defect rather than curing it, and every field the answer reads — `index`, `kind`, `label`, the two edge ends — is one `research/raw/m039-render-phase.json`’s `/effect/freshRead` already holds. That is why the milestone takes no capture, and why this record names a record rather than a route it drove.

The record does not measure what the pane looks like. The five sentences it renders are enumerated in `panel-tutor-signals.ts`’s `PANE_SENTENCES` and measured for copy in `research/raw/m048-surface-copy.json`, which this record names as a source; this record names the states and the field each reads rather than reproducing the sentences’ rendering.

The record pins no total for the route table or the `LOADERS` map: a later milestone appends to both on purpose, and a recorded total would go stale without changing what this record says about this route.

The record does not claim the demo’s `tutor-signals` fact was written by this task. It is T004’s, it is cited here as the read that reaches the pane (:824), and `panel-demo.spec.ts` holds it to the join’s answer over the record on every test run; this record states the same answer from the same two sources and does not restate the fact.
verdict: measured: /tutor-signals is one lazy route — the `PANEL_SURFACES` entry at :84, spread into `appRoutes` by the one mapped literal at :144-:148 and costing the list no cited line (PLAN C3) — whose `data.surface` names the `tutor-signals` key of `panel-demo.ts`’s `LOADERS` (:65), and that key is the only path to `panel-tutor-signals.ts`: the demo looks it up (:717), awaits the import (:723), calls the module’s default export with the sample fact (:724) and sets the state (:725) and the lines (:726). The pane renders the join’s four states and one absence of its own: `answered` reads `state`, `question`, `effect.label`, `effect.index`, `effect.namedBy`, every `reads[]` member, every `unplaced[]` member, `ordering`, every `claims[]` member and `detail`; `graph-unreadable`, `no-render-entry` and `no-effect-node` each read `state`, `question`, `claims[]` and `detail` — with `unplaced[]` beside the third — and `no-tutor-signals-answer` reads no field at all. The ordering is the named absence `no-write-record-no-order`, stated in its own sentence (:196) on every answer, because no write record exists in `extension/` and an edge carries no field to order a write in. The answer shipped is the join’s own over `research/raw/m039-render-phase.json`’s `/effect/freshRead`: the effect node labelled "" at index 5, the one upstream node `count` at index 2, no unplaced reference and 3 claims — a different answer over that record than the `render-phase` pane renders, derived node-side and not read off a page.
